body:
Slice **4b of 7** of #635 (the re-slicing of the old 4-of-6 after its 5th Do iteration was
sent back to Plan on 2026-07-31 — one bundle was carrying three separable kinds of work and
each round surfaced a fresh batch of blockers at ~2.8x its line budget). Depends on #650.

Sibling slices of the old #651: **#651** (4a — restore + desired-state, the two
`gc::ReferenceSet` consumers) and **4c** (`repoint_chunk` + the record ceilings + the
repair/evacuation write path).

## What

The three maintenance passes that scan `inode:` **themselves** — reconstruction, backfill and
rebalance — read a chunk map through the shared resolver (`metadata::resolve_chunk_map`,
#649) with per-object containment, and nothing more. This slice is the **read side only**:
no pass here writes a segmented record.

On #650's tree these three still fail closed at seven sites, so a single segmented object
aborts the whole pass:

| Site | Pass |
|---|---|
| `crates/custodian/src/reconstruction.rs:331` | `assess` |
| `crates/custodian/src/reconstruction.rs:582`, `:635` | `find_chunk` |
| `crates/custodian/src/backfill.rs:98`, `:180` | fill scan + the rewrite |
| `crates/custodian/src/rebalance.rs:161`, `:258` | evacuation scan + plan |

Also in scope, because it is the finding still open at #647's close: `assess` calls
`find_chunk` **per queued chunk** and `find_chunk` resolves **every** scanned object, so the
deployed repair loop is Q namespace scans x N point reads. Resolve once per object per pass.

## Out of scope

- **any write to a segmented record** — a repair or evacuation whose chunk lives in a `seg:`
  record is *refused and stays queued*, and the pass reports non-certifying. The CAS that moves
  such a placement (`repoint_chunk`) and the record ceilings it needs are **4c**;
- restore and `desired_state` (#651);
- the chunk-id floor (#652); the committer, fence, rollback and resume (#653);
- any new/edited ADR / spec / proposal; any conformance-vector change.

## Constraints carried forward (blockers found on the old #651, must not recur)

- **Bounded memory.** A pass must not retain the whole namespace's decoded chunks and every
  segment's exact bytes; memory must not grow with total segmented metadata, nor
  O(chunks x segments) by deep-copying a segmented root into each plan.
- **Containment on *any* read fault, not just `ChunkMapError`.** A serde decode failure on a
  concurrently-replaced root must contain that object, not abort the walk — the containment
  invariant this slice exists to restore.
- **A duplicate committed chunk id is ambiguous**, repaired by neither reference, and both
  objects are named.

## Acceptance

- a store holding a segmented object no longer aborts a reconstruction / backfill / rebalance
  pass; the seven `SegmentedMapUnsupported` sites above are gone;
- a repair obligation for a chunk living in a `seg:` record is **not** drained as "referenced by
  no committed chunk map" — it stays queued;
- a committed object whose map cannot be read is **named**, the walk continues past it, and the
  pass answers `Reconciled::Blocked` — never `Satisfied`; a queued repair for a *healthy* chunk
  in the same pass is still assessed;
- backfill leaves a segmented record **byte-identical**, declining with a stated reason on the
  audit seam and a counted gauge, while a *fillable flat* record in the same store is still
  filled in the same pass;
- reconstruction resolves each object's root **once per pass**, asserted as O(N) not O(Q x N)
  on a *counted* instrumented store double;
- `cargo xtask ci` green.

Part of #635 / #508 / epic #513.

milestone.description: First tagged release (Alpha). Scheduled after the two production-metadata milestones complete: #14 (Metadata Store FoundationDB) and #5 (M4 — Production metadata backend) — i.e. after the FDB go/no-go (#442) records go, the default flips to FDB, and TiKV development stands down (#443).
